page.overview:
What is Church?

A church , clinic, sanctuary, revive pool, or House of Life, is a means of reviving party members in the first three Final Fantasy games. Reviving characters in a church usually costs a small fee. Later, Phoenix Downs and Raise became the main sources of revival, and so the concept of churches or revive pools were scrapped except as plot devices.

Churches (Clinics in the North American NES version) are found in every town and village on the world map except Melmond, which is said to be destroyed by the vampire. The cost of reviving a party member increases as the more levels a party member reaches throughout the game. Talking to the priest will make two angels descend upon the fallen party member(s) and revive them, at which point the angels will depart. This scene does not appear in the Pixel Remaster version of the game.

In the original Japanese Famicom of the game, the churches had the Christian cross on top of the building. This is changed to a heart symbol in the NES release, likely due to Nintendo of America's censorship policy at the time of the release. Later versions remove the cross from the church without any replacement. Additionally, the priest found inside of the church wears a mitre with a Christian cross on it. The mitre is removed in the NES release and instead depicts the priest as having a bald head; later versions retain the mitre but removes the cross on it.

Sanctuaries are found in most towns and villages on the world map. They appear as unmarked buildings with a statue of a goddess inside. Examining the statue will revive all KO'd party members in the party with 1 HP at no cost. Two angels will descend upon the fallen party member(s) and revive them, at which point the angels will depart. The FMV opening also briefly features a church steeple, which is seen collapsing during the Fall of Fynn.
